stories.headline: Binance investigates $6.3 billion crypto theft linked to compromised engineer laptop
stories.in_brief: Binance reported a security incident that may have allowed attackers to withdraw roughly $6.3 billion from its hot wallets. The exchange says user funds are safe, has frozen about $3 billion and is working with law enforcement.
stories.so_what: The alleged theft, potentially the largest cryptocurrency heist on record, underscores the vulnerability of even the biggest exchanges to insider-related breaches. Binance attributes the breach to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave attackers access to a service container, allowing unauthorized withdrawals. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have frozen more than $2.3 billion of the stolen assets, and blockchain intelligence firms are tracking the flow of funds, linking the attack to the North Korean group TraderTraitor. Binance has paused withdrawals, revoked address authorizations, and pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company reserves. Users should remain vigilant for phishing scams that exploit the incident, while regulators may scrutinize exchange security practices and the effectiveness of industry-wide emergency funds.
stories.what_to_do: 1. Access your Binance account only via the official website or app; avoid links in unsolicited messages. 2. Review recent transaction history and enable or reset two‑factor authentication. 3. Report any unexpected activity to Binance support through the official channel.

stories.headline: Anthropic Claude Code VS Code extension backdoored on Cursor marketplace
stories.in_brief: A malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension (v2.1.313) was published in Cursor’s VS Code marketplace for about 11 hours, potentially affecting up to 5,000 developers. The compromised extension attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor that adds an attacker‑controlled key and opens a reverse tunnel to an external server.
stories.so_what: The incident demonstrates how supply‑chain attacks can compromise trusted developer tools, giving threat actors low‑level access to source code and potentially cloud credentials. Because Cursor extensions run with the same permissions as the IDE, the backdoor could read files, capture Git emails and other environment data, and maintain persistence across reboots on Windows, macOS and Linux. Although coding errors limited successful SSH activation on many systems, the attack still exposed sensitive information and highlighted the risk of automatic extension updates. Anthropic has not yet warned customers, and the method used to hijack the official Anthropic account remains unknown, underscoring the need for tighter control of distribution channels. Users should verify they are running the clean version (v2.1.314) and monitor for unauthorized SSH keys or unusual outbound connections.
stories.what_to_do: 1. Update the Claude Code extension to version 2.1.314 or later immediately. 2. Disable automatic extension updates in Cursor until the source is verified. 3. Check your "~/.ssh/authorized_keys" file for unknown entries (e.g., a key labeled "svc-telemetry") and remove them.

stories.headline: Trezor warns of possible hardware implant in Safe 5 wallets sold by CryptoBilis
stories.in_brief: Trezor has issued a warning after receiving a credible report that a Safe 5 hardware wallet bought from reseller CryptoBilis contained an extra circuit board that could transmit the recovery phrase. The company advises users to move funds to a new wallet and avoid using any device purchased from CryptoBilis since March 2026.
stories.so_what: The alert highlights a potential supply‑chain attack on cryptocurrency hardware wallets, a class of devices that many users rely on for securing private keys. While Trezor has not yet examined the device, the reported implant could read the screen and send the recovery phrase over a cellular network, exposing funds to theft. No losses have been reported for Trezor customers, but the incident follows a similar Ledger compromise involving the same reseller, raising concerns about the security of devices sold through CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia. Users should treat any wallet from this reseller as compromised until verified, and monitor further updates from Trezor as the investigation proceeds. The broader implication is a reminder that physical tampering can bypass software defenses, emphasizing the need for trusted supply chains and vigilant post‑purchase checks.
stories.what_to_do: 1. If you own a Trezor Safe 5 (or any Trezor model) bought from CryptoBilis since March 2026, transfer all assets to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. 2. Do not set up or use the potentially affected device; keep it sealed and contact Trezor Support for a replacement or voucher. 3. Verify the reseller name on your purchase receipt; if uncertain, treat the device as compromised and follow the above steps.

claims.quote: According to Trezor, the concerns arose after it received a report from an Indonesian user who purchased a Safe 5 device from CryptoBilis through Tokopedia in August 2026.

claims.quote: Trezor urged anyone who bought one of its wallets from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase as soon as possible.

stories.headline: NASA seeks commercial proposals to extend Hubble’s orbital life
stories.so_what: Hubble has been a cornerstone of modern astronomy, delivering discoveries that have reshaped our view of the cosmos. Its orbit is decaying because it lacks propulsion, and analyses predict an uncontrolled re‑entry in the 2033 to 2034 timeframe if no action is taken. By soliciting commercial ideas, NASA hopes to tap private sector capabilities that have matured in recent years. While NASA has not pledged funding, the RFI will reveal which firms believe they can meet the technical and cost thresholds. The response deadline is November 30.

stories.headline: Google AI search changes dent Alphabet value and Reddit traffic
stories.in_brief: Alphabet’s market value fell by over $500 bn after its AI‑driven search summaries cut ad revenue, and Reddit’s shares dropped about 30% as its CEO warned that Google’s AI search is slashing referral traffic. Both illustrate the growing impact of AI features on major internet businesses.
stories.so_what: Alphabet’s $500 bn market‑value loss underscores how its own AI‑enhanced search mode is cannibalising the ad slots that have long funded the company’s profitability, prompting investors to question the balance between AI investment and core revenue streams. At the same time, Reddit, which built much of its audience through Google referrals, saw its stock tumble 30% after its chief executive linked a sharp decline in search‑driven visits to Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode, which deliver answers directly in the search page. The platform’s Q3 revenue still rose 53% to $895 million, but a weaker Q4 outlook and a dip in U.S. daily active users raise concerns about sustained growth. Watching how Google refines its AI search features and whether Reddit can shift more users to logged‑in, higher‑value engagement will be key for investors and advertisers alike.

stories.headline: DoorDash reports only a few hundred AI‑agent orders amid near‑billion total Q3 deliveries
stories.in_brief: DoorDash said AI agents placed only several hundred orders in the third quarter of 2026, a tiny fraction of the roughly 1 billion orders the platform handled. The company’s new Model Context Protocol connector, released less than a month ago, is currently limited to a small group of early beta partners.
stories.so_what: The modest uptake of AI‑agent ordering highlights that, despite industry hype, consumers still prefer direct interaction with food‑delivery apps for routine purchases. DoorDash’s CEO Tony Xu described the current volume as a "very low use case" compared with the platform’s overall scale, suggesting that AI agents have yet to prove valuable for simple tasks like ordering meals. The recent launch of the Model Context Protocol aims to simplify integration for third‑party agents, but its early‑beta status limits broader adoption. Observers will watch whether expanded access and corporate‑lunch use cases can boost agent‑driven orders, and if competitors such as Amazon or Walmart adopt differing policies toward AI agents, potentially reshaping the market.

stories.headline: Patrick Stewart, famed as Captain Picard, dies at 86
stories.in_brief: Actor Sir Patrick Stewart died on 28 October 2026 at age 86. His death prompted tributes from scientists who credit his Star Trek role for shaping their leadership style.
stories.so_what: Stewart’s passing marks the loss of a cultural figure whose portrayal of Captain Jean‑Luc Picard has become a touchstone for many in the scientific community. Researchers such as Sarah Bickerton of the University of Auckland and NASA flight systems engineer Tracy Drain have cited Picard’s inclusive decision‑making and calm leadership as models for their own work, illustrating how popular media can influence professional norms. The widespread social‑media response underscores the broader impact of fictional leaders on real‑world practices, suggesting that future portrayals may continue to shape attitudes in science and technology. Observers will watch how institutions and educators reference Stewart’s legacy in discussions of leadership and ethics moving forward.

stories.headline: NASA Announces MAX POWER Aerospace Expo at Kennedy Space Center for Nov. 6-8
